I inspected the sample app (local files) to determine which areas matter (vector search, index creation, connection handling, secrets, client reuse, auditing). I then searched the official Microsoft documentation for Azure DocumentDB (vector-search, connection, indexing, transactions, monitoring, role-based access) and recorded the most relevant practices (P01..P37). For prior beliefs: where an Azure DocumentDB public documentation page explicitly matched a prior belief, I marked that belief as confirmed and attached the prior belief id/text into the matching discovered practice entry (examples: K01->P01, K02->P02, K03->P03, K04->P04, K06->P05, K07->P20, K08->P08, K09->P09, K10->P12, K11->P14, K15->P11, K18->P10, K19->P13, K20->P06, K21->P35, K23->P16). For prior beliefs where I could not find a public Azure DocumentDB doc that supports or contradicts them, I marked them as prior_knowledge_only and recorded the searches I ran (these items are: K12, K13, K14, K16, K17, K22, K24). The app itself (README, src/seed_data.py, src/agents.py) demonstrates several local best practices (env var usage, synthetic embeddings fallback, creating a vector index via driver where possible) which I recorded as local_file-sourced practices (P19, P25, P30).
